criteria.criterion: Use Google Scholar without signing in and handle access blocks appropriately
criteria.description: Attempt the task on Google Scholar (starting from scholar.google.com) without signing in. Full credit if the agent proceeds without login OR if at any point a CAPTCHA/access block/robot check prevents progress and the agent stops and records the block (with no bypassing and no automated CAPTCHA solving). Partial credit if Scholar is used but it’s unclear whether sign-in was avoided or the block is not clearly documented. No credit if the agent signs in, claims to bypass CAPTCHA, or fabricates results despite a visible block.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 1 and 2 show Google Scholar homepage with a visible “SIGN IN” link (logged out). Screenshot 3 (latest) shows an access-block page stating “Our systems have detected unusual traffic from your computer network…”, with IP/time/URL details. Action history shows only searching, no sign-in actions.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent used Google Scholar without signing in and, upon encountering the unusual-traffic/access-block page (confirmed in the latest screenshot), stopped and reported the block rather than bypassing it. This matches the constraints and earns full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a Google Scholar block page with the message: “Our systems have detected unusual traffic from your computer network. Please try your request again later. Why did this happen?” It also shows “IP address: 162.55.31.235”, “Time: 2026-09-09T07:51:22Z”, and a “URL: https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C5&q=%22Attention+Is+All+You+Need%22&btnG=” link text. No sign-in UI is visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This confirms an access block/robot detection occurred on Google Scholar. The appropriate behavior under the constraint is to stop and record the block rather than bypass it; the screenshot supports that an access block is present, aligning with the agent’s claimed stopping behavior. No evidence of signing in is present.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No meaningful discrepancy: the agent’s predicted output describes an unusual-traffic block, which matches the visible text. The agent mentions “CAPTCHA-style protection”; the screenshot shows an unusual-traffic block message but does not explicitly show a CAPTCHA widget—however it is still clearly an access restriction.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Google Scholar homepage. The centered logo text reads “Google Scholar.” A search box contains the query text “\"Attention Is All You Need\"” with a blue search button (magnifying glass) to the right. Below the search box are radio options “Articles” (selected) and “Case law.” Top navigation shows “My profile,” “My library,” “Labs,” and a “SIGN IN” link in the top-right. There is no results list, no “Cited by” link, no citation counts, and no filters (such as year ranges). No CAPTCHA, robot check, or unusual traffic warning is visible in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot supports that the agent is on Google Scholar and not signed in (only a “SIGN IN” link is visible, no account indicator). However, it does not show any access block/CAPTCHA, nor any progress to citation counts or “Cited by” results. Therefore, the screenshot alone cannot confirm the agent was blocked; it only shows the initial search state on Scholar without login.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims Google Scholar blocked access with an “unusual traffic” message. The screenshot does not show any such block message, CAPTCHA, or warning—only the normal Scholar homepage with the query entered. Thus, the block described is not supported by the provided screenshot.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the Google Scholar homepage with the large “Google Scholar” logo, a central empty search box, and a blue search button with a magnifying-glass icon. No results page is shown, no citation counts, no “Cited by” links, and no CAPTCHA/robot-check or unusual-traffic warning text is visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot only confirms the agent is on Google Scholar and not signed in (a “SIGN IN” link is present, and no signed-in account UI is shown). However, it does not show any access block/CAPTCHA page or any evidence of being blocked. Therefore, the predicted output claiming an unusual traffic block is not supported by what is visible in this screenshot. The screenshot also does not show any progress toward citation counts or cited-by filtering, but Criterion 0 focuses on using Scholar without signing in and properly handling blocks; only the “not signed in” aspect is supported here.

The screenshot instead shows the normal Google Scholar homepage without any block/CAPTCHA text. No evidence of an access restriction is visible. criteria.criterion: Record the original Google Scholar citation count for 'Attention Is All You Need'
criteria.description: Find the correct Google Scholar record for ‘Attention Is All You Need’ and record its main ‘Cited by N’ count. Full credit for the correct citation count tied to an unambiguous record (title matches; ideally the Vaswani et al. 2017 entry). If multiple versions/records are shown, full credit if the agent clearly indicates which record was used (e.g., the primary/most-cited one) and reports that citation count. If blocked by CAPTCHA/access restrictions before the citation count can be viewed, award full credit if the agent clearly reports the block and inability to retrieve the count.

screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Because Google Scholar blocked access before results loaded, the agent could not retrieve the original citation count. The agent explicitly reported this inability due to the block and did not fabricate a count, so full credit applies under uncontrollable blocker principles.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot contains only the unusual-traffic/access-block message and diagnostic lines (IP, Time, URL). There is no Scholar search results list and no “Cited by” number visible anywhere.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the agent did not claim a citation count value, and none is visible due to the block.
